newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher on Tuesday, recovering from recent bad U.S. news on technical buying and lack of selling pressure.
Five to 10-year paper was leading both the price rise and the volume charts as this segment is seen outperforming in a flattening trend which many dealers regard as unavoidable.
After last week's rate cuts in low-yielding Europe, the curve has become even steeper, but the underperformance of the long end was seen overdone as inflation risks were minimal.
Dutch July CPI published on Friday rose 2.1 percent year-on-year, below 3.0 pct which is regarded "safe".
"Pressure at the long end is caused by the weak performance of U.S. Treasuries and last week's rate cuts at a time of economic recovery, which could fuel inflation," one dealer said.
But as economic growth in Europe would not be outrageous and government budget control also helped to tame price hikes, jitters were overdone, another said.
Trading concentrated in 2001s and 2002s, including the new September 2002 benchmark.
"One big investor with a square position is covering while the state has 1.4 billion guilders of the new 2002s left on the shelf and is selling in bits," one trader said.
Trade was dominated by professionals, but retail investors were also in the market, buying the new 2002s at cheaper levels than last week's closing issue price of 100.35.
"Investors should nurture their guilder bonds, because selling pressure is hardly visible," one dealer said.
Another said that the yield on the January 2006 benchmark should bounce back to 6.18 percent from today's 6.28 percent.
But not many dealers dared believe in further gains, which could be warranted by low inflation risks and a low cost of carry with the new key money market rates.
"We're at historically low levels. That creates an important mental barrier," one dealer said.
